name: Manoj Kumar
current_role: Whole-time Director, RSPL Ltd (RSPL Group, Kanpur); oversees the group's dairy business
profile: Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani is the elder son of RSPL founder-chairman Murli Dhar Gyanchandani and a promoter/whole-time director of RSPL Ltd (since 2008), maker of Ghadi detergent. The Kanpur-based group has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear (Red Chief), real estate and 50+ MW of wind/solar power; Manoj runs the dairy arm.
interesting_fact: RSPL operates wind and solar plants across India generating over 50.1 MW of renewable energy, alongside its FMCG business that employs 25,000+ people.
deep_cut_fact: Ghadi broke into a Nirma/Surf-dominated market by making its detergent white (rivals were yellow or blue), with the tagline 'Pehle istemaal karein phir vishwas karein' (First use it, then trust it).
notes: Hurun lists him as 'Manoj Kumar'; company registry (DIN 00049387) shows him as Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani, whole-time director of RSPL Ltd. Family is notably low-profile; only the general corporate inbox is published. RSPL renewable-energy arm is a possible energy-podcast angle.

name: James J Goetz
current_role: Partner, Sequoia Capital; independent director of Palo Alto Networks (since 2005) and Intel (since 2019)
profile: Jim Goetz is a Sequoia Capital partner (since 2004) who led the firm's investment in WhatsApp, sold to Facebook in 2014, and backed Palo Alto Networks, AdMob, GitHub and HubSpot. Earlier he co-founded VitalSigns Software (sold 1998) and worked at Accel. He stepped back from Sequoia management in 2017 but still invests and sits on boards.
interesting_fact: Sequoia was WhatsApp's only outside investor; Goetz led that bet, and he topped the Forbes Midas List of venture capitalists every year from 2013 to 2017.
deep_cut_fact: His family bought the 1915 Los Gatos Theatre in 2011 as a philanthropic project, seismically retrofitted and renovated it, then donated it (plus two adjacent shops) to the Town of Los Gatos in 2021.
notes: Electrical/computer engineer (Univ. of Cincinnati BS, Stanford MS); gave $25M to UC in 2021. His Sequoia bio says that for his first six months there he silently shadowed Michael Moritz, Doug Leone, Don Valentine and Pierre Lamond to board meetings. Best route is through Sequoia.

name: James R. Scott Jr
current_role: Director, First Interstate BancSystem (since May 2025); Managing General Partner, JS Investments LP
profile: James R. Scott Jr. (48) is a member of the Scott family that founded First Interstate Bank and remains a major holder under the Scott Family Stockholder Agreement. A career banker, he worked at Citywide Banks in Denver and then in First Interstate's commercial banking in Missoula, Ashland (OR) and Denver before rejoining the board in 2025 (he also served 2016-2022).
interesting_fact: First Interstate traces to 1968, when founder Homer Scott Sr. bought the Bank of Commerce in Sheridan, Wyoming; the company is now a multi-state regional bank still anchored by the Scott family.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than starting at the top, he worked through the family bank's commercial lending ranks: VP in Missoula (2014-17), Commercial Loan Manager in Ashland, Oregon (2017-19), and Commercial Group Manager in Denver from 2022. He also sits on the Padlock Ranch Company board.
notes: The email belongs to First Interstate's corporate secretary, Kirk D. Jensen, and is published in the 2026 proxy for shareholder questions. It is not a direct line to Scott. He is a low-profile director with no personal public channels found. Holds degrees from CU Boulder (Leeds) and the University of Denver (MBA and MS Finance). He is a director of the Homer and Mildred Scott Foundation.

name: George T. Haber
current_role: Serial semiconductor entrepreneur and investor; listed as Growth Partner at AnD Ventures (unverified aggregator listing)
profile: George T. Haber was born in Oradea, Romania, in 1954 and trained in electronics at the Technion. He worked at Daisy Systems, Sun and SGI, then founded CompCore Multimedia (sold to Zoran for about $80M), GigaPixel (sold to 3dfx for $180M in 2000), Mobilygen (sold in 2008) and CrestaTech, which made TV tuners. He has since invested through the Cresta Fund.
interesting_fact: He says CompCore's technology for playing films on PCs fed into DVD: 'I can say with my hand on my heart that the DVD was, in part, developed by us.'
deep_cut_fact: As an 11th-grader in Oradea he played in a rock band with future actor Adrian Pintea. When the band was short-handed one Friday, he brought a tape recorder and tapes and ran what is reputed to be the city's first disco, earning about 100 lei a night.
notes: His current role is unclear. TheOrg (unverified) lists him as Chairman and Chief AI Officer at TBRS, Chairman of Tailent and Growth Partner at AnD Ventures; MarketScreener lists him as CEO of Adimos Systems. Confirm before outreach. The LinkedIn link comes from his Romanian Wikipedia article. He has also advised Bitdefender and sat on the boards of Romanian tech companies Interakt and Avangate.
